# workflows

## Purpose
GitHub Actions for the justUp PR gate, multi-architecture Docker Hub release, MkDocs Pages deployment, and a weekly security rescan of the published image.

## Files
| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `ci.yml` | Push gate on all branches, PR gate on `main`, manual dispatch, and reusable release gate (`workflow_call`). Eight jobs: `python` (vendored SSLyze wheel preflight, runtime install from `docker/requirements.lock`, locked-wheel resolution for amd64+arm64, dependency-lock consistency, Ruff check + format, parallel pytest `-n auto`); `container` (`docker/entrypoint.sh` and `docker/nmap-worker.sh`: `bash -n` + shellcheck; `docker build --check`); `frontend` (ESLint + Stylelint via `npm run lint`, `node --test` via `npm test`); `browser-matrix` (the strict shell viewport matrix `@layout|@audit-self-test` in Chromium and WebKit, split by `--shard=1/2` and `2/2` into the required checks `Browser matrix (shard 1/2)` and `Browser matrix (shard 2/2)`; every test runs in exactly one shard, JUnit `browser-shell-<n>.xml` and artifact `browser-matrix-<n>` per shard); `browser` (GridStack interactions in Chromium, strict Chromium modal plus the notification-row, wizard and SMTP tests (39 in three specs) with JUnit output, the chart zoom reset, public hostname, endpoint and port picker checks (`@combined-zoom-reset|@public-hostname-ui|@target-endpoints|@portpicker|@endpoint-state|@combined-legend|@recipients-search|@recipient-channels|@recipient-signal-recheck|@traceroute-map|@reset-confirm|@availability-clip|@targets-live-update|@smtp-link-field|@spooler-log|@combined-note|@edit-target-save|@network-diagnostics-layout|@public-egress|@service-detection|@downtime-widget-link`, Chromium and WebKit), the tab, load stability, card and chart clip checks (`@settings-tab-press|@tab-style|@edit-target-tabs|@load-stability|@card-corners|@card-overlays|@combined-clip|@downtime-history|@dashboard-metrics`, Chromium and WebKit), focus/cursor/targets-search checks (`node tests/layout/run.mjs --focus`, Chromium and WebKit), sidebar transition, notification dropdown and authentication browser checks); `manifest` (reject reintroduced `VERSION`/`requirements*.txt`, version is release-shaped); `workflows` (actionlint with shellcheck available); `source-scan` (Trivy fs secret/misconfiguration scan using a checksum-verified release binary). |
| `docker-build.yml` | Runs only for version tags or manual dispatch on a tag. Validates the tag and ancestry, calls CI, builds and smoke-tests both architectures, verifies the Nmap build (version, provenance, TCP/UDP scan), the Nmap worker (see below), libsignal packaging and runtime-image purity, verifies the Nmap worker, scans images, publishes `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME/justup`, builds a run-specific candidate index (`candidate-<version>-<run>-<attempt>`), verifies it, then publishes the version tag and `latest` (`moves_latest`) from that verified index digest, removes temporary tags, and creates a GitHub release. |
| `security.yml` | Weekly (Monday) and manual, read-only rescan of the published `latest` index: each platform child (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) is scanned by digest with the release Trivy policy (same action SHA, `CRITICAL,HIGH`, `ignore-unfixed`, `scanners: vuln`, `.trivyignore`). No registry login (public image), no build, tag or push. A red run means the published image needs a new release. A newer prerelease is not covered because `latest` never follows it. Untested until the first Actions run. |
| `docs-build.yml` | Builds `docs/mkdocs.yml`, scans the resolved docs dependencies, checks links, and deploys from `main` to GitHub Pages. A successful release also triggers a refresh, built from the current head of `main` (never the release commit). |

## Working here
- The application version comes from `pyproject.toml`. The release tag must be `v` plus that version.
- Pin third-party actions to verified full commit SHAs with version comments. In the image and docs scans the reviewed Trivy action revision sets the scanner default; never use `version: latest`. The `ci.yml` source scan pins Trivy itself (`TRIVY_VERSION` plus SHA-256 of the release asset, `skip-setup-trivy`).
- Keep `permissions` minimal, release concurrency serialized, and `is_newest` fail-closed. An older tag must never move `latest` or prune a newer release.
- `meta` declares the build matrix once (step `matrix`); `build` consumes it and `create-manifest` requires exactly those architectures in the digest and toolchain files before publishing. `tools/release-newest.py <tags-file> <version> <arch>...` takes the architectures from that matrix (fragment tags `<version>-<arch>` are not releases) and yields `is_newest` (no newer release of any kind; gates the tag cleanup) and `moves_latest` (stable and newest stable; gates `latest`). A prerelease never moves `latest`. Neither the version tag nor `latest` is touched before the candidate index passed `tools/verify-manifest.py verify` (platforms and pushed digests); both then point at the candidate's index digest (`imagetools create` from digest, no rebuild) and are verified again.
- All Docker Hub access (login, paginated listing, delete with optional absence polling) goes through `tools/dockerhub.py` (stdlib only, tested in `tests/test_dockerhub.py`); credentials via env, a listing error never yields a partial result. The release policy (keep the current version and `latest`) stays in the `cleanup-dockerhub-tags` job.
- `cleanup-arch-tags` runs `always()` and derives its tags from `meta` outputs only: `<version>-<arch>` for every matrix architecture plus the run-specific candidate tag. It never reads artifacts, deletes nothing else, treats an absent tag as fine and fails on any other deletion error. A rerun of the same tag stays possible for the temporary tags (the fragment tags are overwritten, the candidate is unique per attempt), but the published version tag is immutable: `Publish version tag` asks `tools/dockerhub.py exists <version>` first; if the tag exists, the index must carry exactly the digests built in this run (`verify-manifest.py verify`), which confirms it without republishing (and `latest` then follows the existing index digest), otherwise the run fails and the changed components need a new version. Immediately before `latest` moves (`Promote latest`) and before the destructive cleanup (`cleanup-dockerhub-tags`) the registry listing is read again and `release-newest.py` decides again; a contradiction with the `meta` decision fails the job instead of acting (a residual race between that check and the action cannot be closed without registry-side locking).
- `create-release` needs only `meta` and `create-manifest`: tag pruning runs after manifest verification but a pruning failure turns the run red without blocking or undoing the release. Trivy reports (validated by `tools/trivy-report.py`: a non-empty `Results` list with an OS target, never defaulted to zero findings) and the release asset upload (Trivy reports and the per-architecture `toolchain-<arch>.txt` dependency manifests) are mandatory; only a missing CHANGELOG section falls back to a hint text.
- Nmap and traceroute: `meta` resolves the stable Nmap release and its source SHA-256 (`tools/nmap-release.py`, PGP-verified once before any build). Traceroute runs on Nmap, so `mtr` must be absent from the image. The worker runs under its own non-root UID with only `NET_RAW` (ambient); the web process gets no raw-socket rights. After the smoke test, `tools/verify-nmap-worker.py` checks binary, capabilities, scan, trace and supervisor restart inside each image, and the Nmap provenance file is uploaded as artifact `nmap-provenance-<arch>`. Passing it in Actions is the only release evidence for arm64. The archive verified in `meta` (plus signature and signing keys) is uploaded once as artifact `nmap-source`; `create-release` runs `tools/nmap-release.py release-assets`, which re-verifies the signature, compares the archive hash with `NMAP_SOURCE_SHA256` and every `nmap-provenance-<arch>.txt`, and writes `nmap-source-manifest.txt` (with the `create-manifest` output `index_digest`); a mismatch or missing file fails the release. Archive, `.asc` and manifest become release assets; the archive never enters the runtime image.
- Atomic release (`create-release`, the only job with `contents: write`; `tests/test_workflow_contracts.py` pins this): `tools/release-publish.py` decides and verifies, `gh api` does the calls. `manifest` hashes `release-files/` (exactly the expected assets: source archive, `.asc`, `nmap-source-manifest.txt`, and per architecture `trivy`, `toolchain`, `nmap-provenance`, `nmap-sbom`, `nmap-nvd`); `plan` looks at the tag: no release -> create a draft, unpublished draft -> resume (only its stale assets are deleted and re-uploaded), published and complete -> change nothing, published with a missing, different or extra asset (or two releases for one tag) -> fail without touching it. After the upload the draft's assets are downloaded and `verify --draft --downloads` compares state, size, API `digest` and SHA-256; only then the release is published (`draft=false`, `make_latest` from `moves_latest`) and verified again. The tag must already exist (pushed by the maintainer); the workflow never creates, moves or deletes it. Before the registry push the `build` job runs `release-publish.py source` on the downloaded `nmap-source` artifact. Unproven until the first release run: `gh api --slurp`, the `uploads.github.com` upload through `gh api --input`, and the `digest` field of release assets.
- NVD gate (`tools/nvd-gate.py`, tests `tests/test_nvd_gate.py`, exceptions `.nvdignore`): the `build` job writes a CycloneDX SBOM from the image provenance (Nmap and the bundled libraries with purl and, where NVD has one, CPE) and asks the NVD CVE API for CRITICAL CVEs before the push. Exit 1 (CRITICAL) and exit 3 (NVD unreachable or malformed) both fail the job. Only Nmap and libpcap are covered; libdnet and liblinear have no NVD CPE and are reported as `NOT COVERED`. Trivy cannot do this (no NVD CPE matching for generic components). Optional secret `NVD_API_KEY` raises the rate limit. Accept a false positive only in `.nvdignore` with a reason. Details: `docs/development/release-image.md`.
- Docker images use the `justup` repository. The smoke test supplies a test-only `SECRET_KEY` and checks `/healthz` on port 8000. The Dockerfile supplies its own healthcheck.
- libsignal is built from source for both architectures (Dockerfile stage `libsignal-build`). After the smoke test, `tools/verify-libsignal-native.py` runs inside each image and (with `--load`) checks the packaging, the ELF64 little-endian header and that the extracted `libsignal_jni_<arch>.so` can be dlopen()ed with `RTLD_NOW`, which catches a glibc or shared-library mismatch between build and runtime stage. It does not run `JNI_OnLoad` or load the library in the JVM (the jlink runtime has no compiler or jshell, and signal-cli has no offline command that loads it); a real Signal send stays a manual gate.
- Runtime-image purity (`tools/verify-runtime-image.py`, contract in its docstring, tests in `tests/test_runtime_image_purity.py`) runs for each architecture after the libsignal check and before the registry push: `fs <arch>` inside the container and `layers <docker save archive>` on the runner. Allowed: Python and modules, native `.so`, signal-cli and JARs, the jlink Java runtime, application and metadata. Forbidden: gcc/g++/cc/clang/cmake/make/cargo/rustc/rustup/javac/jar/jlink/jdeps/jshell in a bin directory, `~/.cargo`, `~/.rustup`, `.cache`, `/usr/lib/jvm`, `.git`, `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`, `.o`/`.rlib`/`.obj` and static `.a` files, test caches, build credentials, files left in `/tmp`, `/var/tmp`, `/usr/src`. Exceptions: `.a` inside site-packages (numpy) and objects in the CPython `config-*` directory. pip (the base image ships it) must be absent from the final file system (`fs` check: `pip`, `setuptools`, `wheel`, `pkg_resources` in site-packages, `pip*`/`wheel` in `/usr/local/bin`); its bytes remain in the base-image layers, which the layer scan accepts by design (a stricter contract needs a different base image, an open owner decision). The layer scan finds artifacts that a later layer deleted but ignores whiteouts and `/tmp` (its cleanup is the point; the `fs` check owns `/tmp`). The JVM's `/tmp/hsperfdata_*` is removed in the Dockerfile RUN that starts it. Run against the Dockerfile `runtime` target on amd64 locally; arm64 is verified only in Actions.
- The `frontend` job installs with `npm ci --ignore-scripts` and runs `npm run lint` (ESLint over `app/static/js`, Stylelint over the tracked `app/static/css/*.css`) and `npm test` (`node --test tests/js/*.test.mjs`). The `browser-matrix` job runs the Playwright Test layout matrix and audit self-test in both engines as two shards (`--shard=N/2`, 522 tests at the time of writing; do not run the matrix in `browser` as well). The `browser` job installs locked Python dependencies, Node tooling, Chromium and WebKit, runs GridStack interactions in Chromium, the modal browser gate, then lists and runs the notification-row, wizard and SMTP tags exactly once in Chromium (39 tests across three specs, with JUnit output). The tab, load stability, card, chart clip, downtime and dashboard metric tags (`@settings-tab-press|@tab-style|@edit-target-tabs|@load-stability|@card-corners|@card-overlays|@combined-clip|@downtime-history|@dashboard-metrics`) run in Chromium and WebKit, the focus/cursor/targets-search set (`node tests/layout/run.mjs --focus`) likewise. Sidebar transition, notification dropdown, chart zoom and legend, recipients, route map, confirm dialogs, spooler log, target forms, service detection, public egress, public hostname, endpoint and port picker (`@combined-zoom-reset|@public-hostname-ui|@target-endpoints|@portpicker|@endpoint-state|@combined-legend|@recipients-search|@recipient-channels|@recipient-signal-recheck|@traceroute-map|@reset-confirm|@availability-clip|@targets-live-update|@smtp-link-field|@spooler-log|@combined-note|@edit-target-save|@network-diagnostics-layout|@public-egress|@service-detection|@downtime-widget-link`) run in Chromium and WebKit and authentication browser checks run separately in Chromium. It uploads Playwright JUnit/traces and notification dropdown findings. The full profile and Firefox remain local; missing browser engines fail the strict layout tests. Config lives in `tools/eslint.config.mjs` and `tools/stylelint.config.mjs`, the manifest in `package.json`.
- The toolchain manifest also carries `java_version` and `libsignal_client` (read from `/opt/COMPONENTS.txt`) plus the Nmap fields, so the parity gate compares them across architectures. `tools/toolchain-parity.py` fails on a missing or empty required field (see `REQUIRED_FIELDS` in the script, plus every direct dependency of `pyproject.toml`) even when it is missing everywhere, and on any difference, except the per-architecture fields `temurin_package_version` and `debian_packages` (archived, not compared). Keep other architecture-specific values (library file names, hashes) out of it.
- Resolve the shared Python base digest and signal-cli release in `meta`. The Dockerfile still resolves apt packages and the Adoptium Temurin package during each build; those inputs are not frozen across architectures. Each architecture is built once with `--load`; the tested image is the one tagged and pushed (no second `docker build`), and the installed dependency set is attached to the GitHub release as `toolchain-<arch>.txt`. Hash-locked requirements and SHA-pinned actions are deliberate project policy; Renovate `pinDigests` stays.
- Architectures: the build matrix in `meta` is the only list for the release; `release-newest.py`, the digest checks and the release notes read `archs` from it. `security.yml` repeats the platforms (`EXPECTED_PLATFORMS`; `tests/test_workflow_contracts.py` fails on drift), and the `ci.yml` wheel check loops over wheel platform tags (`x86_64`, `aarch64`) instead: deliberate second lists with different vocabularies.
- `docs-build.yml` deliberately deploys the docs from the current head of `main`, not from the release commit. Its concurrency group is `docs-<workflow>-<ref>` (`scan` for the scheduled run) and cancels in-progress runs only for pull requests, so a deploy is never cancelled by a later push.
- Long inline scripts that need tests live in `tools/` (`verify-manifest.py`, `toolchain-parity.py`, `trivy-report.py`, `verify-runtime-image.py`, `verify-nmap-worker.py`, `nmap-release.py`, `nvd-gate.py`, `release-publish.py`); the release-notes assembly stays inline in the `github-script` step because it needs the GitHub API objects.
- The documentation config lives at `docs/mkdocs.yml`.
- `.trivyignore` is the versioned exception file. Keep an empty file when there are no accepted findings. Used by the image and docs scans; do not delete it.
- `.trivyignore.yaml` holds the one accepted misconfiguration (`DS-0002`, `docker/Dockerfile` only, with `expired_at`) and is used by the `ci.yml` source scan only.

## Validation
- Run `actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml` after edits; it checks inline shell through shellcheck when shellcheck is installed.
- The focused local checks are `bash -n docker/entrypoint.sh`, `shellcheck docker/entrypoint.sh`, `docker build --check -f docker/Dockerfile .`, and `mkdocs build -f docs/mkdocs.yml --strict` after copying the root docs files into a disposable docs tree.
- The `python` job is reproducible locally with `pytest tests/test_dependency_lock.py -q` (supply-chain drift), `ruff check .` plus `ruff format --check .`, and `pytest -n auto`. The focused `@portpicker|@endpoint-state|@target-endpoints` set in `browser` is reproducible with the same Playwright command and `JUSTUP_LAYOUT_BROWSERS=chromium`.
- The `frontend` job is reproducible locally with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, `npm run lint`, and `TZ=Europe/Berlin tools/run-limited.sh npm test`. The tagged notification-row, wizard and SMTP browser set is reproducible with `JUSTUP_LAYOUT_BROWSERS=chromium npx playwright test --config tests/layout/playwright.config.mjs --list --grep '@notifications|@wizard|@smtp-ui'` (39 tests in three specs), followed by the same command without `--list`. The tab, load stability, card, chart clip, downtime and dashboard metric set runs with `JUSTUP_LAYOUT_BROWSERS=chromium,webkit npx playwright test --config tests/layout/playwright.config.mjs --grep '@settings-tab-press|@tab-style|@edit-target-tabs|@load-stability|@card-corners|@card-overlays|@combined-clip|@downtime-history|@dashboard-metrics'`; one matrix shard runs with `JUSTUP_LAYOUT_PROFILE=quick JUSTUP_LAYOUT_BROWSERS=chromium,webkit npx playwright test --config tests/layout/playwright.config.mjs --grep '@layout|@audit-self-test' --shard=1/2` (2/2 for the other).
- Locally, run the `pytest`, `node` and `npx playwright test` commands above only through `tools/run-limited.sh` (root `AGENTS.md`). The unwrapped form shown here is what the workflows execute.
- `verify-manifest.py` rejects more than one index entry per `os/architecture` (variants are not part of the platform contract). The release tools are tested by `pytest tests/test_dockerhub.py tests/test_release_tools.py tests/test_runtime_image_purity.py tests/test_workflow_contracts.py tests/test_libsignal_native_check.py -n 0`; structural GitHub workflow gates are also covered by `node --test tests/js/workflow-contracts.test.mjs`.
- Image publishing, registry tag cleanup, GitHub releases, and Pages deployment run only in their protected GitHub Actions jobs.

- CI and local test limits: the workflows do not use `tools/run-limited.sh` and keep `pytest -n auto` and 2 Playwright workers (`CI` set; `JUSTUP_LAYOUT_WORKERS` still overrides). The local budget from `tools/test-budget.mjs` (see root `AGENTS.md`) is deliberately conservative for shared machines: on a 2 vCPU/7 GB runner it yields 1 worker, on 4 vCPU/16 GB also 1, so adopting it in CI would be slower; CI stays unchanged.
